name: The Willemsplein Plane

location.neighbourhood: City centre, between the station and Sonsbeek park

verified_sources: https://www.monumentaltrees.com/nl/nld/gelderland/arnhem/12308_willemsplein/ (independent listing exists for this tree/location, confirmed via search; page itself 403s automated fetch)
access: Free. Stands on the open public square, visible and reachable at all times.
transport: Arnhem Centraal station, about 5 minutes' walk.
verify_notes: LRMB register (Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen, nr 1677474): planted 1880-1890, so roughly 135-145 years old today (2026). Stands on a prominent spot on Willemsplein, Arnhem's busiest transit square, connecting the station, city centre and Sonsbeek park. Register describes an impressive tree with a broad crown on a very image-defining spot; construction work above and below ground (station-area redevelopment) hurt its condition over the years, so the growing site was enriched and the tree fitted with a semi-automatic watering system. The trunk base was damaged in the past but no longer visibly so; there is a large opening about 5m up leading to a sizeable cavity, and healthy bracket fungi are visible in the crown, so the crown carries cable anchors as a safety precaution. Register rates overall condition as 'reasonable to good' following the growing-site improvements. Gemeente Arnhem's own redevelopment page for Willemsplein (arnhem.nl) confirms 'a couple of big, monumental trees' remain a fixed feature of the square through the 2027-2029 redesign, and a council doc (Ontwerpnotitie Openbare Ruimte Herinrichting Willemsplein) explicitly plans a boardwalk winding between the existing monumental plane trees so they are preserved rather than removed. Flagged only because the second, fully independent source (monumentaltrees.com's own listing for this tree) could not be fetched directly (Cloudflare blocks automated access), though its existence at this exact location and species was confirmed via search. No felling language anywhere; alive and actively protected as of the redesign planning documents (2026).

name: The Nieuwe Plein Plane

location.address: Nieuwe Plein, at the ramp to the Nelson Mandela bridge, Arnhem
location.neighbourhood: City centre, between the station and the Rijn waterfront

access: Free. Stands on the open public square/road verge, visible and reachable at all times.
transport: About 10 minutes' walk from Arnhem Centraal station.
verify_notes: LRMB register (nr 1677473): planted 1880-1890, so roughly 135-145 years old. Stands on Nieuwe Plein, the link between Arnhem's city centre and the railway station, on ground that has been through repeated infrastructure works for the ring road around the centre. The register's own history is unusually detailed: growing-site improvement and protective measures were already needed in the 1970s (a grate kept paving off the trunk base), and when a road tunnel was later dug nearby, the main roots were deliberately routed under the tunnel box to a planting bed 30 metres away rather than being cut. Despite the surrounding traffic and works the register calls the tree in fairly good shape, with little visible damage and still vital in recent years. Owner is the municipality (gemeente), publicly visitable and visible. No felling or death language. Flagged for single-source verification (register only); no independent second source found this pass, searches for the tree by name returned only unrelated Nelson Mandela bridge/Roermondsplein results.

name: The Boulevard Heuvelink Plane
verified_sources: https://www.spijkerkwartier.net/wegwijs/bomen2014.htm (independent neighbourhood tree survey confirms a monumental plane tree stands on Boulevard Heuvelink near this stretch, corroborating existence and monumental status)
access: Free. Stands on the public road verge/footpath of Boulevard Heuvelink.
transport: About 20 minutes' walk from Arnhem Centraal station.
verify_notes: LRMB register (nr 1692447): planted 1880-1900, in the period the famous 'Boulevardplan' (presented 1877 by architect Hendrik Jan Heuvelink jr, based on his father's 20-year-older plan) was largely completed (by 1899). Register calls it a tree in good condition with a strong structure, image-defining for the location, growing fast: it already reached 400cm trunk girth before 2006 and the register projected it would reach 500cm by 2023 (girth recorded here as 400cm, the last dated figure in the source; the 500cm figure is a projection, not a measurement, so not used as girth_cm). The register also notes another registered plane further east on the boulevard near house number 197. An independent Spijkerkwartier neighbourhood tree survey (spijkerkwartier.net, 2014) separately confirms 'the monumental plane tree (around nr. 89)' as a known landmark on this street, corroborating the register's designation from outside the register itself, though it gives no age or measurement of its own. Some root damage noted near the footpath side but otherwise a gave (sound), healthy tree. No felling or death language. Owner is the municipality, publicly visitable and visible.

name: The Agnietenstraat Turkey Oak
verified_sources: data/registers/netherlands-lrmb.json (LRMB register nr 1692437, common Dutch name 'Moseik' verified as Quercus cerris/Turkey Oak via ecopedia.be and other Dutch nursery references)

https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joodse_begraafplaatsen_(Arnhem) (and related local-history sources) independently confirm the register's own claim that this ground was part of the former 'Onder de Linden' cemetery complex (used 1852-1876, cleared by 1959), corroborating the site's history though not the tree itself
access: Free, public green strip (plantsoen) opposite a primary school.
transport: About 15 minutes' walk from Arnhem Centraal station.
verify_notes: LRMB register (nr 1692437): local name 'Moseik', confirmed via independent Dutch horticultural sources (ecopedia.be, arborix.be, vdberk) as Quercus cerris, the Turkey Oak, not to be confused with 'Moeraseik' (Pin Oak, Quercus palustris), a different tree with a similar-sounding Dutch name. Planted 1910, so roughly 110-120 years old. Register history: the tree stands in the green strip on Agnietenstraat, opposite a primary school; at planting time the site was part of the former 'Onder de Linden' cemetery (used 1852-1876), independently corroborated by Dutch local-history sources describing that cemetery's location and closure. A new residential block went up on the plantsoen's east edge in 2017 and the register notes the trees there, including this oak, appear to have come through that construction well, describing it as having a sound trunk and a fine, broad crown. No felling or death language. Owner is the municipality, publicly visitable and visible.

name: The Velperweg Copper Beech

location.address: Viewed from the Rosendaalsestraat car park, off Velperweg, Arnhem (the tree itself stands in a private back garden at Velperweg 31D)

access: View-only. The tree stands in a private garden and cannot be entered (register marks it not visitable), but its full crown is described as visible from the public Rosendaalsestraat car park, with a partial view also possible from Velperweg itself.
transport: About 20 minutes' walk from Arnhem Centraal station.
verify_notes: LRMB register (nr 1690690): planted 1840-1850, so roughly 175-185 years old, considerably older than the 1930s house whose back garden it now stands in; register speculates it may once have stood beside one of the villas that occupied this ground earlier. Register explicitly states 'a small part of the tree can be seen from Velperweg; the full crown is visible from the Rosendaalsestraat car park', which is the basis for treating this as a view-only entry per the site's own rule for trees you can see but not reach: pin marks the viewing place (the car park) rather than the private garden itself, hence location_precision is set to approximate. Register calls it a beech in good condition, on its way to a 4-metre girth as of the last measurement (2006), with no measurements recorded since. No felling or death language. Flagged for single-source verification; no independent second source found this pass beyond general confirmation that the Velperweg/Rosendaalsestraat area and its car park exist as described. Note on the pin: the coordinate recorded here is the register's own tree-level coordinate (the private garden), not a separately surveyed viewing-point coordinate; a later pass should walk to the Rosendaalsestraat car park and record its actual coordinate as the pin, which is why location_precision is set to approximate rather than confirmed despite the register giving exact tree coordinates.

name: The Zijpendaal Giant Arborvitae

location.address: Near the copper beeches, Kasteel Zijpendaal, Arnhem

access: Free, public landscape park and estate (Landgoed Zijpendaal, managed by Geldersch Landschap & Kasteelen).
transport: About 25 minutes' walk from Arnhem Centraal station.
verify_notes: LRMB register (nr 1687995): planted 1900-1910, so roughly 110-120 years old. Stands in Park Zijpendaal (also spelled Zypendaal), a public landscape park and estate whose current garden design dates from 1864 (landscape architect Eduard Petzold); the register is careful to date the tree's OWN planting separately from that redesign, to 1900-1910. Stands close to a group of also-registered monumental copper beeches. Register calls it a large tree of high experiential value, in fair to good condition, and specifically notes its striking layering habit: new stems keep sprouting from the main trunk ('afleggers'), giving it a distinctive, self-made stage of growth. Note for the writer: a similarly named giant arborvitae at nearby Kasteel Rosendael (a different estate, in Rozendaal, about 2.5km further north) is unrelated to this specimen and should not be conflated with it; a WebSearch initially returned that other tree and it was discarded as the wrong location once checked. No felling or death language in this register entry. Owner is the municipality, publicly visitable and visible. Flagged for single-source verification; no independent second source found this pass for this specific tree.
